note: Snake story templates, one list per problem type (PLAN 3.4, Playthrough fixes step 4). Blanks: {snake}, {things} (plural noun), and any number in the problem's data as {key} or {key_things} ("5 crickets"). Lists like a skip-count sequence fill {key} as "5, 10, 15". Count numbers in a story are always 2 or more. The icon is drawn when a story needs a picture to count.

count_objects: The {snake} found some {things} under a rock. How many {things} can you count?
The {snake} is watching these {things}. How many {things} are there?
next_number: The {snake} counted {n_things} on a log. Then 1 more came. How many {things} are on the log now?
There were {n_things} by the {snake}'s rock. Then 1 more came. How many {things} are there now?
compare_more: The {snake} saw {a_things} by the pond and {b_things} by a tree. Which number is more, {a} or {b}?
There were {a_things} on one rock and {b_things} on another. Which number is more, {a} or {b}?
add: The {snake} saw {a_things} by a rock. Then {b} more came. How many {things} did it see in all?
There were {a_things} on a log and {b_things} in the grass. How many {things} were there in all?
subtract: The {snake} saw {a_things} by a rock. Then {b} went away. How many {things} are left?
There were {a_things} under a big leaf. {b} of them crawled off. How many {things} are still there?
missing_addend: The {snake} saw {a_things}. Then some more came. Now there are {total}. How many more {things} came?
tens_ones: The {snake} put {n_things} into piles of 10, with some left over. How many {place} are in {n}?
There are {n_things} near the {snake}'s rock. How many {place} are in {n}?
compare: The {snake} saw {a_things} in one pond and {b_things} in another. Which sign goes between {a} and {b}?
skip_count: The {snake} counts {things} by {step}s: {sequence}. What number comes next?
digit_value: The {snake} counted {n_things} on its long trip. What is the {digit} worth in {n}?
clock: The {snake} wakes up from its nap at this time. What time does the clock show?
The {snake} goes looking for {things} at this time. What time does the clock show?
coins: The {snake} found these coins under its rock. How much money did it find?
equal_groups: The {snake} saw {groups} logs with {size_things} on each log. How many {things} in all?
multiply: The {snake} looked under {a} rocks. Each rock had {b_things}. How many {things} in all?
divide: The {snake} shared {dividend_things} equally among {divisor} friends. How many {things} did each friend get?
missing_factor: The {snake} looked under {a} rocks. Each rock had the same number of {things}. There were {product} {things} in all. How many {things} were under each rock?
